articles.title: Google’s Gemini is now on Android Auto
articles.summary: Google announced that its Gemini AI assistant is now available for Android Auto for help with navigation, errands, or just brainstorming.
articles.body: Move over Google Assistant, there’s a new robot to yell at while driving. Starting today, Google is rolling out its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto users, allowing drivers access to a “truly conversational” voice assistant who can help with directions, messages, and errands. With Gemini, “you can just speak naturally, have a back and forth conversation and get more complex tasks done,” says Guemmy Kim, Senior Director of Product & User Experience, Android for Cars, in a blog post published today. Customers will need to download the Gemini app on their Android phone, which they will then see on their car’s infotainment display while projecting Android Auto. They can then activate the AI assistant by saying “Hey Google,” pressing the mic button on their car screen, or long pressing the voice control button on their steering wheel. To be sure, Gemini is not available for users Apple CarPlay, nor will it be anytime soon. Google spokesperson Sofia Giovannello said the company didn’t have any updates to share on that front. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: For months, Google has been cramming Gemini to a host of platforms it controls, from Chrome to Google Maps to Nest and Google Home products. But Android Auto is among the first attempts to bring the AI chatbot in to the world of driving. Google says that vehicles with its built-in Android operating systems will be next; Polestar, for example, recently announced that a future software update would bring Gemini to its lineup of electric sports cars. Gemini should offer a step change over the current crop of voice assistants, Google claims. For example, you can ask it for help finding restaurants with a specific cuisine, tell it to message your friends with your ETA with an added emoji, check your calendar for events, make a to-do list, and find addresses buried in your emails. And most importantly, you can purportedly do all this while keeping your hands on the wheel and your eyes on the road. Google says that Gemini can also just hang and chat if that’s what you want. According to Kim, the chatbot can “help you learn something new, brainstorm ideas, rehearse for important moments and much more, all in one continuous conversation.” But will this help drivers focus on the task of driving, or just be another distraction? There’s early research that suggests that speech-based voice assistants in the car are associated with “a rather moderate than high level of cognitive distraction.” There is an assumption that anything that helps prevent you from looking at your phone while driving is an improvement, but that might not necessarily be the case. More research will be needed, especially as tech companies rush to introduce more powerful, AI assistants to the in-car experience.

articles.title: Apple’s chip chief might be the next exec to leave
articles.summary: Apple’s chip chief, Johny Srouji is “seriously considering” leaving for another company in the near future.
articles.body: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman is reporting that Johny Srouji, senior vice president of hardware technologies, told Tim Cook he is “seriously considering” leaving Apple for another company in the near future. It was reported in October that Srouji was “evaluating his future at the tech giant.” While nothing is confirmed, it seems the executive is leaning toward not having a future at Cupertino. If Srouji leaves, he would be just the latest in a string of high-profile shakeups in the company’s C-suite. COO Jeff Williams announced his retirement in July, which led to some shifting of roles. But things have only accelerated in December, with AI chief John Giannandrea stepping down, policy lead Lisa Jackson and general counsel Kate Adams announcing plans to retire, and UI design lead Alan Dye departing for Meta, all in the last few days. Apple has struggled somewhat to find its footing as the industry further embraces AI. Now Tim Cook is tasked with trying to stem the bleeding, while being subject to rumors of his own departure. Gurman, who is usually reliable, has said those rumors are premature, but it still adds to the uncertainty surrounding what is typically one of the more stable companies in Silicon Valley.

articles.title: Apple hardware vp Johny Srouji reportedly tells staff “I don’t plan on leaving anytime soon.”
articles.summary:

articles.title: SC: PRF descobre carga clandestina de emagrecedor em bateria de carro | G1
articles.standfirst: Os envolvidos foram detidos e os produtos, apreendidos. O compartimento da bateria do veículo foi adaptado com baterias de moto para esconder os produtos clandestinos.
articles.summary: Os envolvidos foram detidos e os produtos, apreendidos. O compartimento da bateria do veículo foi adaptado com baterias de moto para esconder os produtos clandestinos.
articles.body:
Mais de 60 itens - entre ampolas de emagrecedores, frascos de anabolizantes e cigarros eletrônicos - foram flagrados sendo transportados clandestinamente na BR-101 em Joinville , cidade mais populosa de Santa Catarina , no Norte do estado.

Segundo a Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF),o motorista e o passageiro contaram que alugaram o veículo para fazer uma viagem rápida de ida e volta até Foz do Iguaçu (PR), cidade que faz fronteira com o Paraguai. Os dois foram detidos e os produtos, apreendidos.

Durante a revista pessoal, os agentes encontraram ampolas de emagrecedores escondidas nas roupas dos suspeitos e caixas de medicamentos sob as palmilhas dos calçados.

Ao serem questionados se havia mais irregularidades, um dos ocupantes confessou que existiam outros produtos escondidos sob o capô do carro.

No compartimento da bateria do veículo, adaptado com baterias menores de moto para abrir espaço, os policiais acharam os frascos de anabolizantes. Chaves específicas para retirar a peça estavam guardadas junto ao estepe.

Os dois foram encaminhados à delegacia da Polícia Federal de Joinville.

Segundo a PF, o transporte ou a comercialização de medicamentos clandestinos se enquadra no crime de adulteração de produto destinado a fins terapêuticos ou medicinais. A pena prevista é de 10 a 15 anos de reclusão.

articles.title: Not everyone is loving their new iPhone Duo
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo went on sale just over two weeks ago, but some early adopters have seen enough.
articles.body: For most new relationships, two weeks probably isn’t enough time to decide if you’re ready for long-term commitment. But two weeks with a new phone? You probably know. The iPhone Duo launched just over two weeks ago, and that’s been enough time for a subset of day-one buyers who aren’t loving the phone to make a decision: It’s time to end things. Also, they wanted their $2,000 back. This is to be expected, to an extent; the Duo just isn’t a phone for everyone. It’s an early adopter device — we called it “a messy, expensive good time” — and on top of that, the hinge appears to be suffering some first-gen growing pains. Despite all that, Apple seems to be selling Duos just fine, with new online orders projected to ship in January. As Apple’s customary 14-day return window came to a close, I reached out to a few people to learn more about why they brought their new Duos back. Some of it felt familiar — the outer screen is small, the cameras aren’t great — but other reasons were a little more surprising. Like the fact that the Duo’s whole proposition as a two-in-one device is sometimes a con, not a pro. [Media: “If I can have an iPad in my pocket, that would be great.” So thought Ben Seligson, a content creator, photographer, and now former iPhone Duo owner. After spending some time with the phone, he discovered that having a phone that’s also your iPad wasn’t always ideal. With two separate devices, Seligson told me, “Usually I’d throw a YouTube video on the iPad or throw a podcast up. And then I start cooking dinner and leave my iPad in one spot, but I’d have my phone in my pocket if I got a text, or I needed to set a timer or something like that.” With the Duo, the phone was also the iPad on the counter, so a quick reply became much more of an interruption. Less surprising: A couple of Duo owners I talked to weren’t interested enough in the form factor to try an Android foldable. Not for a lack of curiosity; rather, the iPhone lock-in feels too strong. Michael Hayes, another former Duo owner, says, “I used to flip back and forth between Android and iOS about 10 years ago, and I think I still have a Pixel in a drawer somewhere … Unless something massive changes, I’m locked into the ecosystem now.” Seligson has been tempted by Samsung’s foldables in the past. “A year ago when the Fold 7 came out I was kind of thinking about it,” he says. “But my whole family uses FaceTime; I’m on FaceTime with them all the time. I’ve got the Mac, I’ve got the iPad. So there’s just too many reasons not to try it.” Both Hayes and Seligson switched back to slab-style iPhones rather than other foldables. Fayethe Vongsouvanh, an art director, envisioned using the Duo for editing photos and planning their wedding. They had the misfortune of a cracked screen on the second day of owning the Duo. “At the time, I was at home recovering from hand surgery, so I knew there was no way I was too rough with it,” says Vongsouvanh. They were able to get a replacement quickly, but a number of other quirks led them to return that one, too. Weight was the biggest factor. “The phone is just too heavy and bulky for my daily use,” they say. [Media: Even though things didn’t work out, the Duo seems to have had an impact on the people I spoke to. “There’s a specialness that the Duo has that I kind of miss,” says Seligson. “It felt different, and it didn’t feel like the same phone everyone’s had for the last ten years.” Spending time with the Duo has inspired others to look at old form factors with a fresh perspective. Vongsouvanh enjoyed writing and drawing with the Duo’s inner screen and an Apple Pencil and has been inspired to pick up an older device more often. “I’ll definitely start using my old iPad Pro with a Paperlike screen protector more often,” they say. For Hayes, the Duo led him to downsize. “If there’s one thing the Duo did, it steered me toward the regular Pro instead of the Pro Max this time because it felt comically big after using the Duo.” Maybe small phones have a chance after all. If you’re still waiting for your Duo, there’s some good news; Apple’s holiday return policy kicked in on November 6th, so anyone who’s just getting their phone will have until January 8th, 2027, to return it for a full refund. Even if you don’t end up keeping the phone, you’re probably in for a good time. I’m still using it as my daily driver a few weeks later, and it keeps managing to surprise me with new tricks. But keep an eye on that return window — just in case.

articles.title: New Shaquille O’Neal game show draws ridicule over absurd premise
articles.summary: ‘Can You Hide... Shaq?’ is coming to ABC
articles.body:
Shaquille O'Neal is set to become the unlikely star of a new hide-and-seek-inspired game show, in which contestants will be tasked with concealing his 7-foot-1-inch frame.

The former NBA star will feature in ABC's Can You Hide... Shaq? , hosted by comedian Nicole Byer.

According to Variety , the show will see eight contestants competing to hide the 7ft 1in sports legend in plain sight around Dallas.

The series logline reads: "In the fast, funny and unpredictable challenges, contestants first split into two teams, each with a set mission and time clock.

"The team that completes its mission with the fewest spottings earns immunity for one team member in the next round, who then becomes team captain.

"The teams must work together toward one greater mission: earning prize money to add to the 'Shaq-pot' that will ultimately be claimed by one winner."

Shaq has promised plenty of fun for viewers.

He said in a statement: "I'm 7-foot-1. I'm not exactly easy to miss.

"I love meeting people wherever I go, but for years I've always wondered, could somebody actually make me disappear? Well, we finally decided to put it to the test.

"We turned it into a real competition, and I can't wait for you to see the creative, ridiculous ways they tried to hide me in plain sight.

"The stakes are high, and so is the prize. But you know me, we're gonna have some fun along the way."

On social media, the concept quickly drew ridicule, with one person comparing it to a sketch from 30 Rock .

They shared a photo of Alec Baldwin's network executive character, Jack Donaghy, speaking to Tina Fey's TV writer character, Liz Lemon, alongside the caption: "The premise is simple, Lemon: Contestants must hide Shaquille O'Neal from the people of Dallas. If this works, the network is ready to greenlight similar shows like 'Will You Co-Sign Lenny Dykstra's Loan?' and 'Can You Convince a Georgia Football Player to Call an Uber?'"

Shaq previously revealed how 12 months of success in 1996 forced him to maintain a level of focus that helped shape the rest of his career.

During that single year, Shaquille joined the Los Angeles Lakers after four seasons with the Orlando Magic, represented the United States at the Atlanta Olympics, was selected for the NBA's 50th Anniversary Team, released his third studio album, You Can't Stop the Reign, and starred as a genie in the fantasy comedy Kazaam.

Shaq told People magazine: "That was probably one of my years where I had to be focused every day."

He added: "I'm a guy that likes to go up and down with my focus on purpose, of course, because I always like to get away from it and then get back. But that year, there was so much coming, so much expectation, so many opportunities."

Can You Hide... Shaq? will premiere with two episodes on Thursday, December 3, at 9 p.m. on ABC and the ESPN app. Episodes will stream on Hulu the next day.

articles.title: Sharge’s eye-catching MacBook charger is over 25 percent off
articles.summary: The Sharge Pixel 140 Charger is down to $69.88 ($24 off) right now. You can also score discounts on DJI’s Mobile 8 smartphone gimbal and a Lego-esque Warthog set.
articles.body: Looking for a MacBook and device charger that’s as stylish as it is capable? Both Amazon and Sharge are selling the Pixel 140W GaN charger for $69.88 and $69.90, respectively, a $24 discount on its usual price. If you’re not in need of that much wattage but like the style, Sharge is also selling the 67W version for $19.90 ($30 off) or the 100W version for $59.90 ($16 off). [Product: Sharge Pixel 140 GaN Charger | The Pixel 140 delivers up to 140W of power when using only one of its three USB-C ports, which Sharge says is capable of taking a 16-inch MacBook Pro from a flat battery to 50 percent charge in just 25 minutes. It’s 47 percent smaller than the MacBook’s included charging brick as well, which is great if you’re tight on bag space or travel frequently. The pixel display on the side has configurable brightness and orientation, and displays your current charging wattage. Other deals to consider * Halo fans looking for a fun weeknight project can grab Mattel’s Brick Shop Warthog on Amazon for $62.99 ($12 off), which is the lowest price we’ve seen on the brick-ified UNSC replica. The 935-piece set lets you recreate a 1:22 scale model of the iconic land vehicle, and includes a 1:64 scale metal version as well. * Windows users with Mac Mini envy might consider the Lenovo Yoga Mini, which is currently discounted to $599.99 ($460 off) at Best Buy as part of the retailer’s early Black Friday promo. The compact desktop PC features an Intel Core Ultra 5 processor, 16GB of LPDDR5X memory, and 512GB of storage; it also has several fun features, including automated lighting around the system and Wi-Fi presence sensing. * While modern smartphone camera stabilization has improved dramatically, there are still plenty of situations where a motorized gimbal can help you capture a smoother shot. Fortunately, the DJI Osmo Mobile 8 is currently on sale at Amazon for $89 ($20 off), nearly matching its best price to date. It features 360-degree horizontal panning and over 10 hours of battery life on a single charge.

articles.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders Video Review - IGN
articles.summary: Monster Hunter Outlanders reviewed by Hayes Madsen, played on iOS (iPhone 14 Plus), also available on Android."Monster Hunter Outlanders is simply one of those games that has too much stuff; it's overflowing with mobile-style fluff to keep track of, much of which gets in the way of enjoying that strong gameplay formula it clearly has. In many ways, it's genuinely remarkable how ambitious Outlanders is, and how deftly it manages to adapt the brilliance of Monster Hunter World into a smaller package. The smart streamlining of combat still keeps the intensity of hunts alive, while being more playable in short bursts. And while there's enough good here to keep you engaged, it equally comes with no shortage of frustrations in monetization, roadblocks, and the headache of endless menu management. That means, ultimately, Outlanders doesn't reach the heights of its console counterparts, but if you can go in with tempered expectations, the heart of Monster Hunter is still there."

articles.title: Arjun Bijlani opens up about fatherhood, shares the values he wants to instil in son Ayaan; says, "I feel it’s my responsibility to lead by example"
articles.summary: Actor Arjun Bijlani has opened up about fatherhood and the values he hopes to instil in his son, Ayaan.
articles.body: Actor Arjun Bijlani has opened up about fatherhood and the values he hopes to instil in his son, Ayaan. In an exclusive quote shared with IANS, the ‘Naagin’ actor believes that parenting goes beyond teaching children the difference between right and wrong, as it also involves leading by example.Emphasizing the importance of kindness, respect and empathy, Arjun shared that he wants his son to grow up as a confident, independent and compassionate individual who respects everyone.Speaking about the values he wishes to pass on to his son, Arjun believes that parenting is as much about leading by example as it is about teaching. “I think kindness, respect and empathy are extremely important. As a father to Ayaan, I feel it’s my responsibility to lead by example. Children observe everything we do, so they learn more from our actions than our words. I want Ayaan to grow up being confident, independent, respectful towards everyone and, most importantly, a good human being.”Recalling the things he loved doing as a child, the actor admitted that he sometimes misses the carefree days when life was all about playing outdoors and spending time with friends. However, fatherhood has given him an opportunity to revisit those beautiful moments. “I loved playing outdoors with friends, spending hours doing absolutely nothing and not having to worry about time! I do miss those carefree days sometimes. But now, having Ayaan in my life gives me an opportunity to relive some of those childhood moments. Whether it’s playing with him, enjoying his little stories or seeing his excitement about school activities like Children’s Day, I get to experience that magic all over again,” he shared.Talking about his fondest childhood memories ahead of Children’s Day, Arjun shared, “Children’s Day was always exciting because it was one day when school felt more like a celebration than studies! I remember the fun, performances, games and spending time with friends. Now, as a father, I get to experience that excitement all over again through Ayaan. He looks forward to Children’s Day celebrations at school, and seeing his excitement makes me nostalgic about my own childhood. It’s lovely to see how some traditions never change!”Arjun Bijlani married Neha Swami on May 20, 2013. The couple are parents to a son, Ayaan Bijlani.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: I tried Google’s AI glasses and Meta’s finally got real competition
articles.summary: The Android XR experience is better thanks to Gemini, Google’s privacy protections are more proactive, and Warby Parker and Gentle Monster add style.
articles.body: It’s a weird time to launch a new pair of smart glasses. These last few years, Meta has been the dominant player in pushing a fragile smart glasses resurgence. Unfortunately, its privacy reputation led to the “pervert glasses” moniker. Smart glasses have never been more unpopular. But in the past week, I’ve been demoing some new smart glasses from Samsung, Warby Parker, and Gentle Monster. Some are retro chic frames. Others have the same Y2K vibe as the Matrix films. All were made by Samsung and have Google’s Gemini built in via Android XR, Google’s platform for smart glasses and mixed-reality headsets. The AI demos are better than I expected. In one, I’m sitting in an avant-garde art installation as creepy heads float above my head. On the loudspeaker, words blare in French, Spanish, Korean, and German. Pressing two fingers to my temple, Gemini starts translating each language seamlessly in real time. In another demo, a TV chef cooks a “monster pasta” recipe in Korean while people have a conversation behind me. Music in another language is playing overhead. This exact scenario tripped up the Meta Ray-Ban Display’s translation capabilities when I was on vacation. Here it’s no big deal. I don’t even have to specify the languages I need translated or, as with Meta’s glasses, download a specific language pair to translate. I sit at another table with an English speaker, a Thai speaker, and the glasses translate everything they say to me — correctly — into Japanese. [Image: Gentle Monster’s styles have a bolder, Y2K vibe. But I was most surprised that the glasses automatically redact faces from any photo or video to protect bystander privacy. I asked Gemini to identify my video director, Owen Grove. Gemini told me it knew I was looking at a person, but it can’t identify him because of privacy protections. We pull up a picture of our editor-in-chief, Nilay Patel. There, too, Gemini said that for privacy reasons, it can’t identify a person from a photo either. Meta’s glasses also can’t do this. But what’s striking here is that Google is making an active choice to take facial recognition completely off the table. The Warby Parker and Gentle Monster glasses have the customary privacy LED light that lights up whenever there’s an intent to save visual data. Like Meta’s glasses, there’ll be protections in place to disable the glasses if tampering is detected. However, when I sit down to chat with Juston Payne, Google’s senior director of product management for XR, he says Google intends to go much further than the LED light. “Somebody might come up with some solution [to tamper with privacy LEDs] that our algorithms can’t detect, so then the question becomes: So what can we do?” says Payne. “We’re not going to target ads on it. We’re not going to train Gemini on it. Humans aren’t going to be able to use it to improve the models. We’re also redacting faces before they actually go to the server in the first place, which then gets ahead of certain things that can obviously go sideways if you don’t take those steps proactively.” It’s not just faces that’ll get redacted either. Payne tells me that ambient noise — like bystander conversations — will also get scrubbed. The glasses will only process audio from the glasses-wearer using beam-forming mics. Camera and mic access will also require opt-in permissions. [Image: This photo was taken on a Gentle Monster pair. The camera is 12MP. Alone, these are a bold departure from Meta’s approach to smart glasses. Locally redacting faces and ambient audio, for example, is a conscious choice to give up a valuable source of training data. Google could leave it at that, and Android XR would already have a leg up in the privacy discussion. But Payne says Google plans on using its entire platform to disincentivize glassholes. For example, YouTube will crack down on any creepy videos featuring harassment or unwanted sexualization, regardless of how they’re captured. Google Shopping and Google Ads won’t allow sales or ads for accessories like lens covers for privacy LED lights. Google Play policies will prohibit third-party apps from enabling social livestreaming, real-time facial identification, or changing anything about how the LED light functions. Payne also says third-party apps requiring camera or mic API access will need further review to prove they’re being used responsibly. This is less of a concern right now, but it’s a future-focused stance for other Android XR devices or even with devices like Xreal’s Aura glasses. It’s hard to gauge how effective this privacy policy will be with the public. We’ll have to see how it’s received. It’s much more expansive than Meta’s more reactive approach so far. Granted, Meta doesn’t have its own app store or a computing platform quite like Android. This still underscores how much more Meta could’ve been doing all along. The one area Meta truly nailed with smart glasses has been style. The company, through its partnership with EssilorLuxottica, has over 100 combinations of frames and lenses. Samsung’s partnerships with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster aren’t too shabby to look at. Warby Parker has three designs and three colors: green, brown, and black. Gentle Monster has six frames — including two that are very Y2K — with bolder designs, colors, and tinted lens options. The Warby Parker collection starts at $395, while Gentle Monster starts at $449. Style-wise, I found both collections were fetching. Warby Parker was a bit more everyday, whereas Gentle Monster felt a bit more editorial and runway-ready. Most people should be able to find a look that fits their needs. The glasses are fairly lightweight (for smart glasses) at 41g. Battery life is estimated at around nine hours, while the cases support up to seven extra charges. Sound quality is pretty good, and the 12MP ultrawide camera takes decent photos and video with image stabilization. So, head tilters rejoice! Your accidental Dutch-angle photos will be straightened. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Media: Where Android XR excels is that Gemini on the glasses is, so far, more capable than Meta AI on the Ray-Bans. I was able to look at an event flyer for a concert in Mumbai, have Gemini add the details to Google Calendar, and then look up flight details to India. It gave me turn-by-turn walking directions while also telling me the event schedule for the Whitney Museum. Beginning a live translation doesn’t require me to download a specific language pair onto my phone like with the Ray-Bans. I was also surprised to see Gemini occasionally correct itself in real-time when it made a mistake, or ask me to get a different view of an object I was trying to identify so it could deliver a more accurate answer. Low-vision and blind users aren’t left out either. The glasses feature Google’s Guided Vision, which offers conversational audio descriptions of environments and surroundings. Android XR is also collaborating with Aira, which allows users to stream what they’re seeing using the camera to a real-time human interpreter. At launch, this particular feature will be for Android users only, but otherwise the glasses will work regardless of your phone. [Image: Warby Parker’s collection is more everyday chic. Leaving my hands-on, it’s never been clearer that technology isn’t currently the issue with smart glasses. Whether or not this form factor takes off will boil down to culture, privacy, and usefulness. And on that front, this space has been stagnating a bit because Meta has been the sole big player setting the tone and pushing the conversation. The Android XR approach is notably different, and serious competition for Meta is excellent for consumers. All that’s left is to see whose approach wins. You can preorder Gentle Monster and Warby Parker smart glasses starting today, and the devices are expected to ship starting December 10th.

articles.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns, chipmaker names CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia gets a new chief executive, days after former CEO Jensen Huang admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as president and chief executive of Nvidia, the company said on Thursday, just a few days after he admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy, sparking a U.S. national security crisis.

In a regulatory filing , Nvidia said its board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday.

Nvidia said its current chief financial officer and executive vice president, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO until the company finds a permanent successor. Kress will continue to serve as the company’s CFO.

Nvidia’s shares were down nearly 12% in early morning trading on Thursday. Since Friday, the company’s stock has fallen by as much as 19%, resulting in a market cap loss of more than $855 billion.

Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it as CEO ever since. Under his leadership, Nvidia played a crucial role in developing the graphics processing unit (GPU), a specialized chip that does graphics processing for PCs, as we know it today. The chips were not an immediate hit, and the early days of Nvidia were characterized by struggle and layoffs, but eventually, it struck on a GPU design that performed so well, it became the standard for graphics processing.

These chips also turned out to be extremely good at doing large numbers of calculations simultaneously, which has made them popular for computation-intensive tasks like crypto mining, and more recently, training and running neural networks, which are what AI models are at their core.

Nvidia was initially focused on making GPUs aimed at gaming, but it had already moved into general-purpose computing by 2006 with the launch of the CUDA architecture, which lets developers use the chips for other tasks, such as doing calculations and research. After AI researchers began using the company’s GPUs to train neural networks over a decade ago, Huang leaned in toward developing chips for AI and then data centers, and grew it from there into its dominant position.

Under Huang, the company has been by far the biggest beneficiary of the AI industry’s skyrocketing growth, which has largely depended on Nvidia’s GPUs for training and running large language models. Before ChatGPT launched and sparked the AI boom, Nvidia shares were trading at about $15. As of last month, they had risen more than 1,450% to an all-time high of $243. Its market cap consequently has also risen by an eye-watering $5.5 trillion since then, reaching as high as $5.88 trillion early in October.

Revenue, of course, has also ballooned, rising more than 1,500% to $96.22 billion as of the company’s second quarter, from $5.93 billion in Q3 2023, right before the ChatGPT moment. Profits increased nearly 88 times in that period to $59.69 billion as of July 2026, from $680 million in October 2023.

That success was predicated on large part by the AI industry’s continued development, which Huang seemingly made his personal mission. He traveled to conferences and events around the world to promote his products and AI, lobbied extensively for looser regulation after the Biden administration placed export controls on the sale of high-power AI chips to China, and cultivated a close relationship with Trump, often to Nvidia’s benefit .

The resignation and controversy come at a crucial moment for Nvidia. China was always a big market for the company, though its impact on the company’s finances has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. Chinese customers accounted for revenue of about $7.9 billion in the company’s second quarter, roughly 8% of total revenue.

The potential implications of Huang’s departure for the AI and data center industries are vast, given how active Huang, and by extension Nvidia, has been in furthering the AI boom. In particular, it raises questions about the future of Nvidia’s sprawling AI investments, which have helped bankroll everything from startups developing new technologies to the enormous data centers needed to run them.

Under Huang, Nvidia deftly used its financial muscle to support companies buying its chips, effectively helping to finance the market for its own products, as well as lobbying Washington to relax potential rules around AI and data center regulation.

As of the end of its second quarter, Nvidia reported $99 billion worth of investments and another $25 billion of commitments. It also has $36 billion in cloud service commitments, which are arrangements that help AI cloud operators finance the GPUs and data center equipment they buy from Nvidia, with the chipmaker saying it will buy compute from them and potentially earn a share of their operators’ revenue.

Nvidia has also been investing directly in neoclouds, the companies serving a lot of the AI processing needs. In January, the company invested $2 billion in CoreWeave , and another $2 billion in Nebius in March. The chipmaker was said to be considering being a guarantor for Nscale’s planned West Virginia data center project. It’s also signed up to provide up to $105 billion worth of credit guarantees for an OpenAI data center campus in Ohio.

Nvidia’s also a major investor in the labs building the AI models that run on its GPUs, putting $30 billion into OpenAI, and $10 billion into Anthropic . It’s also backed Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab as part of a deal involving at least 1 GW of its Vera Rubin GPU systems. The chipmaker has also invested $3.5 billion in MediaTek to help the Taiwanese company develop custom AI chips that work with Nvidia’s systems.

Many investors have grown uneasy with the enormous amounts of debt companies in the space were raising to sustain the AI infrastructure buildout, and Huang’s exit throws another uncertainty-shaped wrench into the works. CoreWeave’s shares were down about 9% on Thursday, reversing part of a 25% rally on Wednesday, while Nebius is down about 16%. IREN fell 6.6%.

Nvidia’s board has also appointed Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993. As chair, Jones is likely to play a central role in Nvidia’s search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang.

Huang is the single largest personal shareholder at Nvidia, but he owns only about 3.5% of the company’s shares. Unlike many of Silicon Valley’s tech giants, he does not hold supervoting rights, and the board had the power to vote him out at any time.

Huang famously ran a very flat organization, with around 60 direct reports. There was no heir apparent or succession plan either (although two of his children also worked in executive roles at the company). Huang famously maintained tight control over the company he founded, making it challenging for Nvidia to find a path forward without him.

The industry will get its first glimpse of that next week during the quarterly conference call. Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday.

“Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the company said in a statement.

Note: This story was updated to add details about Nvidia’s growth and Huang’s efforts to promote AI development, as well as its focus on China.

articles.title: Lego’s BrickLink marketplace has been offline for a week following ‘unusual activity’
articles.summary: BrickLink, Lego’s online marketplace for reselling parts and sets, has been down since November 5th with no estimate of when it will return.
articles.body: Bricklink, a popular online marketplace that Lego bought in 2019 where fans can buy and sell parts and sets, has been down for a week and the company doesn’t know when it will return. The team who runs the site has been sharing updates over the past week including estimates of when it will be back up. It was last expected to return on November 11th, according to Jay’s Brick Blog, but a statement Lego shared to the site yesterday says there’s currently no estimate of when BrickLink will be back online. Lego hasn’t explained exactly what happened with the marketplace, but says it “took BrickLink offline after identifying unusual activity on the platform. Our immediate priority was to secure the site, protect our members and ensure the integrity of BrickLink.” There are also no specifics on when BrickLink will return, as Lego works to contain what happened. “Before bringing the site back online, we need to fully understand what has happened. That means containing the issue, investigating how it happened and checking for related issues.” Three years ago, BrickLink experienced a similar issue around the same time of year resulting in the marketplace being offline for several days due to a cybersecurity incident. Lego shut down the site “out of an abundance of caution” after receiving a “threat and ransom demand.” When BrickLink returned, users were prompted to change their passwords with stronger requirements, but were assured their accounts had not been compromised during the incident.

articles.title: A power bank that can quickly charge three gadgets is just $49

articles.body: Amazon Prime subscribers can jump on a pretty nice deal happening on Ecoflow’s laptop power bank that can deliver up to 140W of power through either of its two USB-C ports. You can snag the limited-time deal happening on the black or silver-colored models for $48.99 (originally $85.79) at Amazon. The 25,000mAh / 90Wh battery is TSA-approved, and can supply a total of 170W to up to three devices sipping from it at once. [Product: Ecoflow Laptop Power Bank | Based on specs alone, this is a fantastic value. It’d be a great fit if you own a USB-C chargeable MacBook or Windows laptop, along with a tablet, gaming handheld, or other devices you use every day. We like to recommend laptop-class power banks whenever prices drop, though they often don’t go below $80 or so for this combination of power, ports, battery capacity, and a built-in screen to monitor output. Compared to something like Anker’s popular Laptop Power Bank, the Ecoflow model is missing on really just one nicetie: built-in cables. Also, it doesn’t seem to include a USB cable, so you’ll need to provide your own. Other great Verge-approved deals * Director Curry Barker’s hit horror film, Obsession, has sunk to the low price of $12.99 at Amazon, Walmart, and Gruv for the 4K Blu-ray. In addition to the 4K disc, the set includes a 1080p standard Blu-ray disc of the film, as well as a digital version. The 54 percent off deal arrives just before the film leaves Peacock on November 17th. It will then likely become more affordable to rent digitally, but snagging Obsession on disc will make for a great stocking stuffer for the horror lover in your life. If you’re a first-time customer at Gruv, you can enter the code FIRSTGRUV15 at checkout to save 15 percent off the order. * Your mileage may vary depending on what you want to shop for, but Amazon’s Resale section (where it displays returned products) is knocking up to 20 percent off at checkout through November 18th. Used goods don’t exactly make for the best gifts, but it’s a savvy way to save some money if you want some accessories. Belkin’s basic, but slim Nintendo Switch 2 case is $23 in like-new condition (originally $29.99), with an extra 10 percent off at checkout. Asus’ promising ROG Kithara open-back gaming headset with Hifiman planar magnetic drivers is 20 percent off its already-discounted $179.33 price at checkout. * The best price you can get on 007 First Light is at Newegg, where the Steam PC edition costs $37.99 without the need for an offer code. IO Interactive’s third-person action game was recently discounted to around $45, but has since returned to its original $69.99 price. With the developer’s lineage in making fun, immersive spy sandboxes with the Hitman franchise, expectations were high that it’d deliver the 007 title that gamers have been craving. Our review didn’t bury the lede, proclaiming right at the top that First Light “captured the franchise’s signature spectacle,” and it delivers a bunch of mission variety to keep the action from getting stale. articles.title: Google Wallet can finally unlock doors with digital home keys
articles.summary: Google has added digital home key support to Google Wallet, allowing Android users to open smart locks by tapping their phone against them or simply approaching.
articles.body: Google has added digital home key support to Google Wallet, allowing Android users to open smart locks by tapping their phone against them or simply approaching. The feature is currently available in public preview for the Google Home app, and will roll out to everyone “over the coming weeks,” according to Google’s announcement. This was a long time coming, given Samsung and Apple users have had this convenience for a while now. While Google Home already has some unlocking functionality, this update allows users to leverage the Near Field Communication (NFC) and Ultra-Wideband (UWB) tech in their phones with compatible smart locks. Multiple locks can be controlled via Google Wallet using a single digital home key. All household members linked to the same Google Home account can also add their own key to their personal Google Wallet. Tap to Unlock works by holding the back of an NFC-enabled Android phone near the lock reader, and doesn’t require the phone to be unlocked. Unlock on Approach needs to be manually enabled in Google Wallet, but can automatically unlock a door when it detects the user walking up. [Image: This is what Google Wallet users will see when they setup a digital home key. There are a few compatibility requirements to bear in mind, however. These new Google Home capabilities are built on Aliro, the open standard designed to let any smartphone unlock any smart lock, but the hardware that supports it is still fairly limited. According to Google’s announcement, the list of supported locks currently includes the Aqara u400, Schlage Sense Pro (NFC at launch and UWB to follow), and Nuki Keypad 2 NFC, with “more locks to come.” Users will also need a Matter-enabled Google Hub with Thread Border Router, such as the 2nd-gen Nest Hub. Tap to unlock requires NFC-enabled phones running Android 9 or later, and hands-free unlocking only works on Aliro UWB-compatible Android phones, such as the Google Pixel 10 Pro series and above. Wear OS smartwatches aren’t supported “at launch,” according to Google, which implies they might be in the future, and that seems likely given that Apple Watch already has similar unlocking features.

articles.title: ‘The end of Tesla!’: Cybertruck diehards turn on Elon Musk after he pulls the plug
articles.summary: Elon Musk is ending Cybertruck production to prioritize the Cybercab, sparking rare backlash from diehard Tesla influencers and loyal fans on X and YouTube.
articles.body: The Cybertruck is heading to that shiny cyber-dumpster in the sky, leaving the folks who built online identities around Elon Musk’s polarizing pickup feeling bereft. Usually, Musk’s fanbase treads lightly around their idol’s mercurial decisions. This time, however, the truck’s demise has sparked rare backlash within the Tesla community — aimed squarely at the guy who signed its death warrant. Troy Meekhof, who posts on numerous social platforms under the moniker “The Cybertruck Guy,” has been vocal about his disappointment in Musk’s decision to wind down Cybertruck production by the end of summer 2027. (The original plan was to start winding down production in the spring, but then Musk decided to extend it a few months.) In a 33-minute video on YouTube, Meekhof argues that Tesla never fully committed to making the Cybertruck a success, citing a lack of advertising, confusing pricing changes, and the decision to shift focus before the truck could fully establish itself in the market. “It feels like they didn’t try to make Cybertruck a success,” he said. [Media: He also had choice words for Musk’s reasons for ending the Cybertruck’s short run to make room at Giga Texas for the fully autonomous Cybercab: “Cancelling all of your best products... in favor of an autonomous platform that remains both software and regulatory constrained... seems like an absolutely terrible idea,” Meekhof vented. The Cybertruck wasn’t the only Tesla product to meet an untimely end — at least according to those with stakes (and often stock options) in the company’s success. Earlier this year, Tesla discontinued the Model S and Model X, two of its flagship vehicles. With the end of the Cybertruck, Tesla is now left with just the Model 3 and Model Y as vehicles you can actually buy. (The Semi is strictly a commercial vehicle, while the Cybercab’s availability as a consumer product remains dubious, at best.) “Cancelling Cybertruck after all the years of getting it to production to ‘make room for CyberCab’ is a lame excuse,” @TeslaXplored wrote on X. “There are like 500 CyberCabs in one city that only Tesla influencers are riding in. Taking away consumer cars instead of building what the people want will be the end of Tesla!” He added, “Very sad what happened to Tesla over the last 5 years.” [Media: Meanwhile, at least one prominent aftermarket company is offering to step in and pick up the mantle. Unplugged Performance, which makes aftermarket accessories, said it would produce the Cybertruck and other vehicles on the truck platform under license, with investors funding the effort: “Worth a conversation?” Musk, for his part, seems less interested in litigating the particulars of Cybertruck production and more intent on selling a vision of Tesla’s future centered around the Cybercab and humanoid robots. “Cybercab will do a majority of all passenger miles in any jurisdiction where it is not prohibited by law,” Musk wrote on X earlier this week. “Obvious to anyone with eyes and a brain.” He also pushed back on claims that the Cybertruck was killed because it was unprofitable. “The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate,” Musk said. “We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people.” To be sure, Cybertruck sales have been disappointing over its entire production run. Musk initially theorized that Tesla could sell 250,000-500,000 Cybertrucks annually, but the actual numbers have been far below those projections. Last year, Tesla is estimated to have sold around 20,000 trucks; the company is on track to sell fewer than that this year. Whether Musk’s autonomous utopia pans out or ends up joining the Cybertruck in the vaporware graveyard remains to be seen. For now, the stainless-steel wedge that was supposed to be the ultimate symbol of an indestructible future has become a monument to Musk’s shifting attention span — and a stark reminder to Tesla’s most loyal boosters that in Elon’s world, nothing should be taken for granted.
